slides.title: Bitcoin, gold or stocks: who won the year?
slides.sub: 12 months of real prices. One winner.

slides.title: The scoreboard
paras: From Oct 17, 2025 to today, the <g>S&P 500</g> is the only one of the three that's up.
Bitcoin is down almost a quarter. Gold is flat, but that hides a wild ride.

slides.title: Bitcoin's rough year
paras: BTC topped near <g>$114K</g> in late October 2025, then slid for eight months.
The low came on June 30: <r>$58.6K, down 49% from the top</r>. It has bounced to about $81.6K since.

slides.title: Gold's round trip
paras: Gold ran <g>+26%</g> to a record <g>$5,318</g> on Jan 29, 2026.
Then it gave it all back: <r>−25% by mid-July</r>. Today it sits right where it started, near $4,180.

slides.title: The pain index
paras: Returns are half the story. The other half: <u>how much it hurt to hold</u>.
Bitcoin's worst single day (<r>−14%</r>) was worse than the S&P's worst stretch of the whole year.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc. from Yahoo Finance daily closes; volatility annualized

slides.title: Zoom out: 3 years
paras: Start the clock in Oct 2023 and the ranking flips: <g>Bitcoin is first</g>, gold second, stocks third.
<u>One year is a short window.</u> Your start date can change the winner.
